          Don't snapshot the working copy, and don't update it

steps.message:
Perfect! I've successfully tracked app.log. Here's what happened:

The file was in `.gitignore` (via `*.log`), which prevented jj from including it in commits. To track it without completely removing the ignore rule, I added a negation pattern `!app.log` to `.gitignore`. This is the minimal change needed to selectively unignore just this file while keeping the rest of the log-ignore rules intact.

The commit "Track log file" now contains:
- **app.log** (newly tracked)
- **.gitignore** (with `!app.log` negation rule added)

This is the standard way VCS systems handle tracking files that would otherwise be ignored—the negation pattern is part of the ignore rules themselves, so you can unignore specific files without removing the general ignore pattern.
